fields.label: bozzuga
fields.description: A squat, wide-mouthed ambusher the colour of wet silt, mottled with salt-white warts, that sits half-sunk in the root-maze channels for days at a time with only its eyes showing. Nothing about it moves until something small comes within a lunge, and then the whole head is mouth. Karrolun, stranded young and anything else small enough to swallow whole are its diet; it has no interest in anything larger. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: fever swarm
fields.description: Individually a fingernail-length, wet-winged thing, gold-dusted and easy to miss. The fever swarm is never seen alone — only as a slow-drifting haze of them, thickest over flowering mangals at the heat of the day. That haze is the green-gold breath the Miasma is named for, seen up close: the same swarm that carries the biome's fevers from pawn to pawn is the only thing that carries pollen between its flowers. You cannot have the trees without the fever. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: karrobel
fields.description: A thick, wedge-bodied scuttler, tapering to a hardened blade of a head it drives into the muck. Rarely seen whole — mostly it is a churned ring of castings and a pair of banded, mud-caked plates breaking the surface. Where it has worked, the ground turns rich: clean delta loam, cast up from whatever the Miasma's sin-soup was before. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: delta loam
fields.description: Clean, fertile soil worked loose and cast up by karrobel burrowing through the Miasma's muck. Where the karrobel have been, the ground turns rich and dark — the one export from this biome that arrives already refined. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes
